module_goal: Build careful listening and auditory discrimination.
Recognise and produce simple rhymes.

module_name: Letter Cluster 1: s a t p i n
module_goal: Learn s, a, t, p, i, n and use them together to build, read, and spell real words.

module_name: Letter Cluster 2: m d g o c
module_goal: Learn m, d, g, o, c and use every letter known so far to build, read, and spell more words.

module_name: Letter Cluster 3: k b h r e
module_goal: Learn k, b, h, r, e and use every letter known so far to build, read, and spell more words.
Learn l, f, u — the last Level 1 letters — and use the full letter set to build, read, and spell words.
Cumulative mixed practice and challenge across every Level 1 letter and word learned.
Demonstrate independent Level 1 mastery across every module.
Read and build core CVC words quickly and confidently before learning new patterns.
Read and spell words starting with two-consonant blends (bl, cl, fl... br, cr, dr...).
Recognise sh, ch, th and wh as single sounds and read/spell words that use them.
Read and spell words ending in -ck, -tch, -dge, -ng and -nk.
Read and spell words with qu and common s-blends/end-blends.

module_name: Letter Cluster 5: j v w x y z
module_goal: Learn the six letters Level 1 never taught, and use them to build, read, and spell more words — including many common sight words.
Read a first set of common words that can't be fully sounded out.
Read and write short dictated sentences using everything learned so far.
Demonstrate independent Level 2 mastery across every pattern learned.
Hear whether a word's vowel sound is short (a quick sound) or long (says its own name) — the listening skill every later Level 3 spelling pattern builds on.
Read and spell words where a final silent e makes the vowel before it say its long sound.
Read and spell words using the ai and ay vowel teams, which both spell the long A sound.
Read and spell words using the ee and ea vowel teams, which both spell the long E sound.
Read and spell words using the oa and ow vowel teams, which both spell the long O sound.
Read and spell words using the oi and oy vowel teams, which both spell the /oi/ sound.
Read and spell words using the ou and ow vowel teams, which both spell the /ow/ sound (as in cow) — with no simple rule for which spelling goes where.
Read and spell words where ar, er, ir, or or ur — a vowel's own sound swallowed by a following r.
Recognise that the same sound can be spelled more than one way (ai/ay, ee/ea, oa/ow, oi/oy, ou/ow, er/ir/ur) — recognition only, never a graded choice between two valid spellings.
Demonstrate independent Level 3 mastery across every pattern learned.
Choose c or k for the /k/ sound at the start of a word, based on the vowel that follows — the first graded spelling choice in the app.
Choose k or ck for the /k/ sound at the end of a word, based on whether a short vowel comes directly before it.
Choose j (not g) for the /j/ sound at the start of a word.
Choose ge or dge for the /j/ sound at the end of a word, based on whether a short vowel comes directly before it.
Choose ch or tch for the /ch/ sound at the end of a word, based on whether a short vowel comes directly before it.
Choose a doubled or single ending letter — f, l, s and sometimes z double after a short vowel at the end of a one-syllable word.
Add -ing/-ed to a word correctly: double the final consonant, drop a silent e, or just add the ending, depending on the base word's shape.
Recognise kn, wr, mb and gn as spellings with a silent first or last letter — receptive only, a new pattern rather than a graded choice.
Recognise y as a vowel at the end of a word — long e in a longer word (happy), long i in a short word (cry).
Choose -s, -es or y-to-ies to make a word plural, based on how the word ends.
Recognise ph as a spelling for the /f/ sound.
Choose un-, re-, -ful, -less or -ly to change a known word's meaning without changing its own spelling.
Demonstrate independent Level 4 mastery across every spelling choice learned.
Choose s, ss, soft c or -ce for the /s/ sound, based on where it sits in the word.
Choose ai or ay for the long-A sound, based on whether it sits in the middle or at the end of the word.
Choose ee or ea for the long-E sound — ee is the more common spelling, ea is a specific set of common words to learn by heart.
Choose igh or ie for the long-I sound, alongside the already-known i_e and y spellings.
Choose oa or ow for the long-O sound, based on whether it sits in the middle or at the end of the word.
Choose ue, ew or oo for the long-U sound, alongside the already-known u_e spelling — oo is the most common, ue and ew are smaller sets to learn by heart.
Hear that -ed is always spelled the same way, but can sound like /t/, /d/ or /id/ depending on the sound before it.
Swap a final y for i before most suffixes (happy to happier), but keep the y before -ing (crying, not criing).
Recognise and spell words with dis-, pre- or mis- at the start, and -ness or -ment at the end, extending Module 39's un-/re-/-ful/-less/-ly.
Choose which member of a word family (e.g. act/action/active/actor) fits a sentence, using the root's job in the sentence as the clue.
Demonstrate independent Level 5 mastery across every spelling choice and morphology skill learned.
Use common Greek and Latin roots (bio, tele, graph, photo, scope, port, dict, spect) as a clue to a word's meaning and spelling.
Recognise and spell rarer long-vowel patterns — eigh, augh, ough and ear for /er/ — as a set of words to learn by heart.
Choose the correct homophone (same sound, different spelling and meaning) based on what the sentence means.
